relationships.subject: AM251
relationships.evidence_quote: The CB1 antagonist AM251 strongly attenuated the antinociceptive effects of CBD/BCP on tactile hypersensitivity in males (Fig 9A) at 60–120 mins post injection

relationships.subject: Cannabidiol
relationships.evidence_quote: Results from this study showed that systemic administration of CBD or BCP individually can dose-dependently reduce SCI-related hypersensitivity in both male and female rats.

relationships.subject: β-caryophyllene
relationships.evidence_quote: Results from this study showed that systemic administration of CBD or BCP individually can dose-dependently reduce SCI-related hypersensitivity in both male and female rats.

key_findings: CBD and BCP co-administration gave synergistic reduction of cold hypersensitivity and additive reduction of tactile hypersensitivity in SCI rats, with minimal side effects.
The combination's antinociception was nearly blocked by CB1 antagonist AM251 but not by CB2 or opioid antagonists.
